text:
Carolina is now three straight wins to the good, and it got there by taking a 3-0 lead before the third period was seven minutes old, then holding on while Columbus came at the Hurricanes in waves. Pyotr Kochetkov, the 2019 second-round pick out of Ryazan-VDV, was the reason it held, and the three stars put him first.

The scoring was quiet early. Jordan Martinook, Logan Stankoven and Mark Jankowski each scored at even strength, and Seth Jarvis set up two of the three. Carolina's early edge in chance quality was real: it held a 1.50 to 0.43 lead in expected goals, a measure of how good each team's shots were, in the first period. But Columbus had the better of the rest. In the third, the Blue Jackets out-chanced the Hurricanes 1.65 to 0.51 and scored twice. Denton Mateychuk made it 3-1 at 6:56, and Kent Johnson cut it to 3-2 on the power play at 9:50.

Over 60 minutes, our numbers lean toward the visitors. Columbus generated 3.17 expected goals to Carolina's 2.35, and in simulated replays of every shot it wins 65 percent of the time. Kochetkov saved about 1.2 goals more than his shots deserved, while Jet Greaves was about 0.65 goals worse than expected. Johnson's best look, a 23 percent chance in the third, went nowhere. For Carolina, that is three in a row, built on a goalie's good night. Columbus leaves with the better underlying game and nothing to show for it.
